summary: Gone 40-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab, built in 1937 north of Priest River, Idaho; abandoned in the 1940s, with only footings and scrap metal left.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 40-foot pole tower
facts.status_note: No tower remains. Idaho Fire Lookouts says only cement footings and scraps of metal are left.

access.note: On Kaniksu National Forest land and listed as drive-up. The level is inferred from the forest and drive-up notes; no source states an access rule.

events.note: 40-foot tower with an L-4 cab. Idaho Fire Lookouts also mentions a log cabin.
Sources give only the 1940s; 1940 is a placeholder for the decade, not a dated event.

evidence.supports: location: about 13 miles north of Priest River
built 1937 as a 40-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab
evidence.quote: Built in 1937, this 40' pole tower with L-4 cab was promptly abandoned in the 1940's.

evidence.supports: built 1937 as a 40-foot L-4 tower and log cabin
evidence.quote: 1937: 40′ L-4 Tower and log cabin were built

evidence.supports: listed as gone on the Idaho list
logging operation; only footings and metal remain
evidence.quote: A logging operation has been thru this area and there is nothing left other than cement footings and various pieces of metal to know there was ever a tower here.

evidence.supports: Mid-Cottonwood Point in Custer County is standing and is a different site
evidence.quote: (Mid-Cottonwood Point) Custer 44.62304 -114.68642 Ground Standing NHLR US 1828, ID 165

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com describes a 40-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab. Idaho Fire Lookouts describes a 40-foot L-4 tower and a log cabin. The story reports both and does not choose between them.
Cottonwood Point is also the name of a standing, registered lookout in Custer County (Mid-Cottonwood Point). That is a different site and is not used in this story.

notes_for_editor: Four short web sources that agree on the core dates. No NHLR or Forest Service record for the Bonner County site was found, so the 1937 build and 1940s abandonment rest on secondary pages. Idaho Fire Lookouts' Our Notes on the logging and footings is undated. Staffing is left out because the only source says no staffing history is documented. The access level public is inferred from National Forest land and the drive-up label. The 1940 abandonment year is a placeholder for the decade. The brief's gone status, design, height, and 1937 build are all supported. This is a different site from the Custer County Mid-Cottonwood Point record (us-id-mid-cottonwood-point).
